claims.statement: Pivotal faces (elementary). With A_i the pivotal set of i and s(x) the sensitivity: (P1) an {i,j}-face is odd exactly when i is pivotal at one end of it and not the other, I(1_{A_i}) = sum_j P(E_ij) and P(E_ij) = 4 P(E_ij, A_i, A_j); (P2) Harper's inequality gives E[s - 1 | A_i] >= (1/2) log2(1/eps_i) (equality for AND_n) and h2(eps_i) <= eps_i log2 e + I(1_{A_i})/2; (P3) any set C of coordinates satisfies sum_C B_t <= sum_C h2(eps_t) <= log2(e) sum_C eps_t + 2 E[s_C (s - 1)], at most (log2 e + 2r) I when at most r coordinates of C are pivotal at a point; (P4) sum_k k W_k(D_i f) = I(1_{A_i})/4 + sum_j P(Par_ij), so the mean level of D_i f is at least (1/2) log2(1/eps_i), with equality for X009's selector. Since P(A_t, A_j) = P(t, j in S), P3 is the sum over C of h2(eps_t) <= eps_t (log2 e + 2 E[|S| - 1 | t in S]): it bounds the trivial witness cost of C and gives nothing below it, so as a rule for leaving C out of a witness argument it is never stronger than sum_C h2(eps_t) = O(I). X009's selector is priced within a factor 1.0076, 1.0003, 1.00001 of its B_t at m = 6, 10, 14 (Harper-tight pivotal set). None of P1-P4 is claimed new: pairwise E[s^2] = E[|S|^2], and the standard mean-level bound (1/2) log2(1/eps) for a function supported on measure eps.

claims.statement: Blocks with signed-character fibers (elementary). If every fiber of F over an address block X is a signed character, F(x, y) = s(x) chi_{tau(x)}(y), then sum_{t in Y} B_t <= H(S_Y) = H(tau(X)) <= 2 I_X, with equality throughout for AND2^N = prod_k (-1)^{t_k (1 - y_k)} (Y the t bits). For any split, B_X = sum_T R_T B(nu_T) with R_T = P(S_Y = T) and nu_T the normalized spectral law of the slice F_T(x) = E_y[F(x, y) chi_T(y)] (on the class, of s 1_{tau = T}). So on the class sum_T R_T B(nu_T) <= B <= sum_T R_T B(nu_T) + 2 I_X: the data block, with any number of unpredictable coordinates (u_t >= u for all t in Y gives sum_Y h2(eps_t) <= (2/u) I), is never the obstruction. The class contains every Boolean function (|Y| = 1), so the address part is as hard as FEI.

claims.statement: K-partite polynomials (elementary). If [n] splits into K blocks and every monomial of the GF(2) polynomial of f = (-1)^P uses at most one variable of each block (the blocks properly colour the graph joining two coordinates that share a monomial), then B <= H <= sum_k H(S_{X_k}) <= 2 sum_k I_{X_{-k}} = 2 (K - 1) I. Every block then has signed-character fibers, and this is exactly the class on which Lemma B (L2-SB) applies to every block at once. With chi the chromatic number of that graph and Delta its largest degree, H <= 2 (chi - 1) I <= 2 Delta I. Sharp at K = 2 (inner product, H = 2n = 2I).

Simulated annealing on shapes up to (4,4,4) and (3,3,3,3), restarted from random sets and from the AND of K bits, found nothing higher; from random starts it often stalls lower, so beyond the exhaustive shapes this is weak evidence that D_3 = c*. A short greedy search over general polynomials of GF(2) degree at most 3 on 5 to 7 variables found nothing above 2.9559 but did not reach c* at 6 and 7 variables either.

best_next_step: B_gap needs a statistic of S - i that carries both scale and count, and it can only be paid on average over coordinates (X009). On read-once AND/OR/parity formulas one integer, the height at which S - i first reaches the branch of i, is exact (L2-R2); on every structured family tried a scale-and-count profile over classes of equal co-occurrence is exact (L2-GW-E); bounded cells lose kappa_h eps_i log(1/eps_i) (L2-R-E). Next: an inequality bounding P(i in S | W) from below on the high-level mass of D_i f for such a W, averaged over i; the scale order must come from the structure, not from co-occurrence alone. And a separate adversarial pass on every CANDIDATE here. Proposition P3 (L2-PF) bounds only the trivial witness cost h2(eps_t), by a spectral second moment, so it exempts nothing the trivial witness does not; the open part is witnesses for the coordinates whose trivial cost is too large. Unpredictable coordinates need not have subcube pivotal sets (L2-PF-E). A data block whose fibers are signed characters is paid by its address block (L2-SB, Lemma B of section 5e): in that class selectors, however many and however unpredictable, are never the obstruction, and the open part is the address part, B averaged over normalized signed subset functions.
